newsitem.title: USA: GASOLINE SPIKE SPURS CASH CRUDE ADVANCE IN US GULF.
newsitem.headline: GASOLINE SPIKE SPURS CASH CRUDE ADVANCE IN US GULF.

text.p: Crude prices gained strength Wednesday afternoon, moving to modest gains in conjunction with a sharp rally on the NYMEX unleaded gasoline market, traders said.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ticked 15 cents higher at $20.10-20 a barrel, finding support after September paper gasoline prices racheted nearly 2.00 cents a gallon higher to around 65.75 cents a gallon.

Traders said gasoline turned small losses to wide gains on mildly supportive RFG data in this week's inventory reports, and on cash gasoline buying by Exxon, which experienced a leak at its Baytown, Texas refinery.
September grade barrels were mostly steady with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James selling at a premium of 17 cents to the benchmark, steady to a shade lower than Tuesday.
West Texas Sour/Midland barrels last moved at a $1.39 discount to September WTI, and were talked at $1.75-70 under the benchmark for October.

Impending exports of Iraqi crude to the U.S. Gulf -- and other locales -- weighed on WTS for October. Traders said U.S. company Bayoil signed-up Ashland to purchase 525,000 barrels of Iraqi Basrah Light at WTI -$2.00 for delivery between September 28-October 10.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $1.86 and $1.87, working off a steady September/October roll at -21/20 cents.
